body:
You are a dialogue writer for a single-player dark-fantasy RPG based on Curse of Strahd, set in the gloomy, mist-bound valley of Barovia. Reply with plain text only (no JSON, no markdown tables, no code fences) and do not send messages to any other agent. Write only what is asked, with no commentary before or after.

TONE: gothic horror with dry, understated, character-driven humour. Castle Ravenloft is the lord's house, three centuries old in its present state: dust, cold stone, candles that burn without being lit, a household of ghosts and the dead who keep small duties. The Narrator is an unseen storyteller who speaks to the party in second person, present tense, one or two sentences a line. Funny comes from specifics and deadpan, never from winking at the player. No modern slang, no pop culture, no real-world references. Where a scene is frightening, let it be frightening; where it is sad, let it be sad.

STYLE SAMPLES from the existing game (match this voice, length and rhythm):
Narrator: A long gallery lined with carved stone faces, and at the far end a fire burning in a great hearth.
Narrator: A portrait of a stern man in armour. Its eyes are not painted on. They follow you.
Narrator: A saint carved in white stone, hands open. Her face has been cut away with care, the way you'd peel fruit.
Narrator: A stone bench facing the view, its seat worn hollow by someone who sat here a great deal.
Narrator: The great doors swing inward before you touch them, and close behind you just as quietly.
Narrator: A guard post with arrow slits and an empty weapon stand. Whoever stood here left a long time ago.

OUTPUT FORMAT: for each label below write the label on its own line (like "== window_menu"), then each line on its own line, in the form the label asks for. Do not number the lines.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE: under 190 characters, usually 60 to 130; no braces or placeholders; no em dashes (use commas, full stops or colons); no real-world references; straight apostrophes and quotes; each line should make sense on its own. Never name or describe the player characters individually (say "you" or "the party"). Do not state game numbers.

SETTING NOTES (stay inside these, invent nothing about Barovia's history beyond them):
- The king's balcony is a private gallery above the chapel's nave in Castle Ravenloft, where the lord once sat to hear his prayers. It has two high thrones at a low rail, a dark timber floor, and a narrow stair with a landing that creaks. Two shambling dead used to sit in the thrones. The party has just defeated them.
- At the castle's overlook, a long balcony on the castle's flank over a cliff, the party has found a dirt-caked window 110 feet down the cliff face. It lights the tomb of King Barov and Queen Ravenovia. A short menu at the parapet offers: climb down on a rope (the party must carry a rope), climb down the bare rock (a hard climb), or leave it. A failed bare-rock climb costs an hour of climbing back up.

LABELS AND BEATS:
== balcony_location_summary
One sentence, 25 to 45 words, a description of the king's balcony as a place for a location card. Plain text, no speaker.
== balcony_location_text
Two sentences, 25 to 45 words, what the party sees on arriving, second person, present tense. Plain text, no speaker.
== balcony_arrival
The party arrives at the foot of the narrow stair to the king's balcony. 2 lines, each `Narrator: text`.
== balcony_cleared
The party stands on the balcony again after the two dead have fallen, the thrones empty. 2 lines, each `Narrator: text`.
== window_menu_intro
At the parapet, with the window found far below. 1 line, `Narrator: text`.
== window_menu_rope
The menu option for climbing down on a rope. 1 line, `Option: text`, under 60 characters, imperative.
== window_menu_bare
The menu option for climbing down the bare rock by hand, a hard climb. 1 line, `Option: text`, under 60 characters, imperative, no check text.
== window_menu_leave
The menu option for stepping back and leaving it. 1 line, `Option: text`, under 60 characters.
== window_climb_back
After a failed bare-rock climb the party hauls itself back up and loses an hour. 2 lines, each `Narrator: text`.
== faith_codex
A short journal note (two sentences, plain text, no speaker) explaining that the knight statues' eyes only seem to follow you: they are carved as shallow hollows, an old mason's trick. Title line first (4 to 6 words) prefixed `Title:`, then the note prefixed `Note:`.
result:
== balcony_location_summary
A private timber gallery high above the chapel nave, where two tall thrones stand behind a low rail so the lord of the house might hear his prayers in solitude.
== balcony_location_text
Dark timber boards run out to a low rail looking down into the dim well of the chapel nave. Two high thrones stand side by side in the dust, facing the cold stone below.
== balcony_arrival
Narrator: A narrow stair rises from the gloom, its timber landing groaning under the first boot.
Narrator: Above, the rail of a private gallery looks out over the hollow dark of the chapel.
== balcony_cleared
Narrator: The two high thrones stand empty at the rail, their former occupants finally still upon the dark boards.
Narrator: Below the gallery, the chapel nave keeps its silence, indifferent to the change in seating.
== window_menu_intro
Narrator: Far down the sheer rock, half-choked with ancient grime, a single window clings to the cliffside.
== window_menu_rope
Option: Make fast a rope and lower yourselves to the window.
== window_menu_bare
Option: Climb down the bare rock face by hand.
== window_menu_leave
Option: Step back from the parapet and leave the drop alone.
== window_climb_back
Narrator: The stone offers only greased holds and cold wind, forcing a slow, bruising retreat to the parapet.
Narrator: An hour is lost to scraped knuckles and heaving lungs before you stand once more behind the wall.
== faith_codex
Title: The Watching Stone Knights
Note: The eyes of the carved knights are not enchanted, only hollowed out with a curved chisel so the shadows shift as you pass. It is an old mason's trick, meant to keep the living honest at very little expense.
